ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Quantization Error Analysis in Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: Analyze the effect of error accumulation in diffusion models via a controlled experiment where we maintain a fixed level of error at each denoising step, but vary the number of steps, and measure the overall output quality.
CONTROLS: Compare to the full-precision model, and include controls for different bit-widths (e.g. 8-bit, 16-bit) to understand the impact of quantization on error accumulation.
COST: 100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the quantization error to not saturate at a fixed point, but rather accumulate nonlinearly across the number of steps, reflecting the interdependent nature of diffusion models. Failure could arise if experimental design does not effectively control for constant error at each step, which would compromise the validity of the analysis.

ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: Efficient Post-Training Quantization for Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: Develop an efficient post-training quantization method that accounts for error accumulation in diffusion models by adding a learnable bias term to each layer, which adapts to the accumulated error from previous steps, and performing joint calibration of this bias term with the quantization parameters using a small subset of samples.
CONTROLS: Compare to existing post-training quantization methods and full-precision models, and include ablation studies to understand the effectiveness of the bias term and joint calibration.
COST: 200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the proposed method to outperform existing post-training quantization methods by up to 2x in output quality at the same bit-width, but may struggle to achieve similar performance at very low bit-widths (e.g. 4-bit) due to the limited expressiveness of the bias term.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Efficient Post-Training Quantization for Diffusion Models
REVISED PROPOSAL: Modify the existing proposal to add a learnable error correction network that can be trained jointly with the bias term and quantization parameters, which can correct for the accumulated error at each step, instead of relying on a fixed bias term. This would increase the computational overhead at training time but potentially allow for better performance at very low bit-widths.
CONTROLS: Keep the same controls as before, and add additional experiments to compare the performance of the error correction network with a simpler approach that uses a fixed bias term.
COST: 250 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the revised proposal to achieve better performance at low bit-widths (e.g. 4-bit), but may increase the computational overhead at training time, which could make the method less efficient for large models.

CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the quantized models to their full-precision counterparts, and include controls for different bit-widths (e.g. 8-bit, 16-bit) to understand the impact of quantization on error accumulation.
COST: 300 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the error accumulation to have a significant impact on the performance of real-world diffusion models, especially in tasks that require multiple denoising steps, such as text-to-image generation and image deblurring.

ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Empirical Study of Error Accumulation in Quantized Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: This experiment compares the performance of a quantized diffusion model against its full-precision counterpart on various real-world benchmarks, focusing on text-to-image generation, image deblurring, and style transfer. We will evaluate the degradation of the quantized models, especially focusing on the contributions of error accumulation across denoising steps versus per-step errors. We use a combination of metrics such as PSNR, SSIM, and FID score to measure the visual quality of generated images and compare them to the corresponding full-precision models.
CONTROLS:  We compare against: (1) a full-precision diffusion model, (2) a quantized model that uses a standard post-training quantization method, and (3) smaller diffusion models with reduced number of denoising steps.
COST: 50 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect that the evaluation will indicate the significant contribution of error accumulation to the degradation of quantized diffusion models. The results may however fail to segment the individual contributions of per-step error accumulation and classical step-to-step noise propagation, and it might be harder to deblur images with higher quantization errors.

ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: Accurately Modeling Error Accumulation in Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: This theoretical result proposes an analytical model to quantify the relationship between the per-step quantization error, the number of denoising steps, and the overall output quality. Specifically, we derive a closed-form expression for the expected value of the overall output error, assuming that each step introduces a quantization error as a random variable. This expression is then analyzed for different quantization schemes and noise levels. The theory assumes that the noise added at each step is Gaussian.
CONTROLS:  We assume that the diffusion model follows a specific architecture and has no additional error correction parameters.
COST: 0 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect that this model will accurately describe the behavior of the quantized diffusion models for mild quantization levels, especially in the low-noise regime. However, it might not capture the effects of the noise propagation and heavy-tailed distributions seen in real-world images, which could lead to inaccurate predictions for moderate to high quantization levels, and especially in complex scenarios such as deblurring.

PROPOSAL: This experiment identifies robust quantization methods that minimize error accumulation while maintaining the visually appealing property of preserving details in recurrent processes, applied specifically to real-world image sequences, primarily dealing with dataset---image deblurring and style transfer. We preserve high-frequency details typically lost during quantization in the early denoising steps to regenerate better real-world particulars. 
CONTROLS:  We compare against: (1) full-precision diffusion model, (2) quantized model with standard post-training quantization method, and (3) variants of our preservation-based quantization with varying storage bit-widths.
COST: 100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect that the preservation of high-frequency details will generate images with both visually pleasing and better new-point and object cohesivesses in many test cases. It might however encounter difficulties to maintain preservation capabilities at high compression levels and in cluttered backgrounds, where noise amplification and pattern distortion become substantial.

ACTION: ADD 4
TITLE: Adaptive Depthwise Quantization for Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: This experiment proposes a new post-training quantization method for diffusion models that adaptively adjusts the quantization bit-width across different channels and denoising steps based on the importance of information in each step. We train a lightweight neural network to predict the optimal quantization bit-width for each channel as a function of the input noise variance and the current denoising step. This method dynamically balances the trade-off between quantization error and computational efficiency.
CONTROLS:  We compare against: (1) full-precision diffusion model, (2) standard post-training quantization method, (3) preservation-based quantization method, and (4) a variant of our adaptive depthwise quantization with static bit-width assignment.
COST: 150 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect that this adaptive method will be able to achieve state-of-the-art results in both image deblurring and style transfer tasks while maintaining a good balance between precision and computational efficiency. However, the results might be sensitive to the performance of the neural network predicting the optimal quantization bit-width. Additionally, the overhead of the neural network might become significant for large models and high-resolution images.

This advanced noise estimation enables more informed quantization decisions and improved overall performance.

However, the additional computational overhead required for noise estimation might be substantial, and the method might struggle to generalize to new, unseen noise distributions or large-scale images.

ACTION: ADD 5
TITLE: Quantization-aware Denoising Diffusion Process
PROPOSAL: This experiment proposes a new, unified framework that integrates quantization-aware denoising into the diffusion process itself. We augment the standard iterative denoising steps with a novel, quantization-aware update rule that adapts to the quantization errors introduced at each step. This approach eliminates the need for explicit post-processing quantization and enables more flexible, adaptive compression strategies.
CONTROLS:  We compare against: (1) full-precision diffusion model, (2) standard post-training quantization method, (3) preservation-based quantization method, and (4) adaptive depthwise quantization method.
COST: 220 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect that this integrated approach will offer improved performance over traditional post-processing quantization methods, especially when combined with the previous adaptive depthwise quantization method. However, the novel update rule might introduce additional computational overhead and require careful tuning to avoid performance degradation in certain scenarios.

ACTION: REVISE 5
 TITLE: Quantization-aware Denoising Diffusion Process
PROPOSAL: This experiment proposes a new, unified framework that integrates quantization-aware denoising into the diffusion process itself. We refine the integrated framework to include a stochastic annealing scheme that dynamically adjusts the trade-off between denoising precision and computational efficiency based on the two evolving probabilistic parameters: the noise variance and the step index. This enhancement enables more efficient compression strategies while maintaining strong performance on various real-world image benchmarks.
CONTROLS:  We compare against: (1) full-precision diffusion model, (2) standard post-training quantization method, (3) preservation-based quantization method, (4) adaptive depthwise quantization method, and (5) a modified version of our earlier adaptive depthwise quantization with stochastic annealing but without quantization-aware denoising.
COST: 250 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect that this enhanced, unified framework will provide a more robust and adaptive solution for real-world image compression and will demonstrate improved performance on deblurring and style transfer tasks compared to traditional post-processing quantization methods and even our own previous methods. However, the performance might be sensitive to the annealing schedule and critically depends on prior extensive hyperparameter fine-tuning.
